learning_outcomes.text: Will know, master, and apply the CTE (Technical Building Code) in the sections corresponding to installations and energy efficiency in buildings.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to energy efficiency in buildings - Introduction and definition
CTE (Technical Building Code) and RITE (Regulations for Thermal Installations in Buildings)
European Directive on Energy Performance of Buildings
Building energy rating - Objectives
Building energy rating - Elements
Building energy rating - Label
Building energy rating - Calculation methodology
Building energy rating - Certification of buildings and homes
Building energy audit - Definition
Building energy audit - Necessary material
Building energy audit - Starting bases
Building energy audit - Planning
Building energy audit - Information processing and definition of improvements
Energy performance of buildings: Heating and Domestic Hot Water (DHW) - Heating and DHW systems
Energy performance of buildings: Heating and DHW - Equipment and installations
Energy performance of buildings: Heating and DHW - Minimum solar contribution
Energy performance of buildings: Heating and DHW - Micro-cogeneration and geothermal energy
Energy performance of buildings: Cooling - Ventilation solutions
Energy performance of buildings: Cooling - Cooling solutions
Thermal insulation of buildings - Facades
Thermal insulation of buildings - Exterior facade rehabilitation
Thermal insulation of buildings - Interior facade rehabilitation
Thermal insulation of buildings - Facade rehabilitation with thermal insulation by injection into cavities
Energy performance of buildings: Lighting systems - CTE-DB-HE3
Energy performance of buildings: Lighting systems - Luminaires
Energy performance of buildings: Lighting systems - Good practices
Measures for energy saving and improving energy efficiency in buildings - Generalities
Measures for energy saving and improving energy efficiency in buildings - Bioclimatic architecture
Measures for energy saving and improving energy efficiency in buildings - Measures for saving and improving energy efficiency
Measures for energy saving and improving energy efficiency in buildings - Reduction of the building's electricity bill
Measures for energy saving and improving energy efficiency in buildings - Future trends
assessment_rules: A minimum of 40% of the total score in written tests is required. If this critical criterion is not met, the final grade for the course will be 'Fail', with the sum of the scores obtained in all assessment systems capped at a maximum of 4.5 points. For part-time students, non-recoverable activities may be replaced by similar ones with a different deadline or equivalent assessment tests, provided the reason aligns with their part-time status.
